This check is informational on pull requests during the pre-launch
burn-down. It gates only the codebase-invariant sections (stub values
and prod-switch coherence). The environment-dependent sections (wiring,
env discovery, operator keys) are surfaced below but do not block the
PR because the runner carries no production secrets. The prod-deploy
gate (deploy-readiness-gate) enforces every section under strict mode.

AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#693 @ 13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

AUD-SOL-PUSH-120, agent 120. A/B/C = 0/4/2.

First full T4 review of all eighteen P2 changed files and the original #648 history; no original APPROVE reused. Prior Sol B-648-8 lease/receipt fencing and B-648-10 quiet-hours preparation-crossing cases now pass, including the previously failing round-4 token-read/handoff-write boundary and urgency/daytime controls; B-648-1 distinct-session/thread cases and B-648-6 deadlines also pass. ([Prior narrowed verdict](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648#issuecomment-5972046897), [Round-4 before proof](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37143855203), [Replayed suites](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37343796456))

### B-693-1 — destination-time dedupe loses a distinct reschedule event

**File:line:** `src/notifications/emitters/booking.emitter.ts:264-279`, together with `push-delivery.service.ts:230-232`. The dedupe key identifies kind/session/**new start time**, not the lifecycle event; returning to a previous destination collides with an earlier, already-sent reschedule. ([Emitter](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Femitters%2Fbooking.emitter.ts), [Outbox](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fpush%2Fpush-delivery.service.ts))

**Executed counterexample:** real BookingEmitter → NotificationsService → worker, same session A→B→C→B, with five-minute gaps and each prior push drained: three inbox records but only **two** provider calls. ([Independent CI](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727))

**Fix rule:** use an immutable lifecycle-event identity or persisted generation for reschedule notifications, stable on replay but different on a later real transition; reminder identities can remain schedule/generation-specific. Simply adding the old time is insufficient for a repeated A→B transition after another cycle. Preserve cross-worker same-event dedupe and add the three-transition and repeated-cycle regressions.

### B-648-7 — reopened in P2: a declared twin is not necessarily a proven twin

**File:line:** `src/packages/drip-dispatcher.cron.ts:511-544`, `src/packages/purchase-fanout.service.ts:670-703`, `src/notifications/notifications.service.ts:489-499`. Both writers unconditionally mark the push row hidden even when their separately guarded inapp write throws or returns null; the sole surviving push row disappears from list/count. ([Drip writer](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fpackages%2Fdrip-dispatcher.cron.ts), [Purchase writer](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fpackages%2Fpurchase-fanout.service.ts), [Hidden-row write](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fnotifications.service.ts))

**Executed counterexample:** the **real DripDispatcherCron writer** encounters one synthetic inapp DB failure, continues as intended, writes its one push-channel row, then the real unread count is **0 instead of 1**; the independently disabled-inapp channel case also fails. ([Actual-writer CI proof](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727))

**Fix rule:** only mark a twin when a successfully committed, qualifying counterpart exists; propagate the actual created-row result/identity, or enforce the counterpart atomically. Failed/suppressed inapp writes must never hide the sole stored notification. Test both writers with throw/null outcomes and the genuine two-row counterpart case; preserve list/unread predicate alignment. This continues the original sole-row-loss finding rather than renumbering it. ([Original B-648-7](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648#issuecomment-5963265503))

### B-693-2 — receipt settlement permanently loses failed token cleanup

**File:line:** `src/notifications/push/push-delivery.service.ts:673-690,713-736`. `clearToken` swallows a DB error, `handleError` reports DeviceNotRegistered anyway, and checkReceipts permanently stamps the receipt checked. ([Exact-head worker](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fpush%2Fpush-delivery.service.ts))

**Executed counterexample:** receipt says DeviceNotRegistered; the first exact-token `updateMany` rejects once, then DB access recovers: receipt sweeps return checked counts **[1,0] rather than [0,1]**, so the known-dead token remains registered and the durable receipt never retries its cleanup. ([Receipt recovery probe](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727))

**Fix rule:** settle only after token cleanup succeeds or a successful exact-token CAS proves that a newer token replaced it. Leave failed cleanup durably retryable, including ticket-stage cleanup; retry cleanup, **not the already-attempted external push**. Keep the existing protection for newly registered tokens.

### B-648-9 — reopened in P2: send preparation can outlive consent

**File:line:** `src/notifications/push/push-delivery.service.ts:462-465,473-514,547`. Preferences are read before later timezone/history/token awaits; the handoff CAS fences only the outbox lease and does not revalidate recipient authorization. ([Exact-head send path](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fpush%2Fpush-delivery.service.ts))

**Executed counterexample:** an initially enabled message enters send preparation, mute commits during a seventy-second token read (still inside the 120-second lease), and the worker subsequently calls Expo **once instead of zero**; the ordinary revoke-before-drain tests pass but do not cover this interleaving. ([Delayed revocation proof](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727), [Passing original deferred-work tests](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37343796456))

**Fix rule:** move/revalidate master/per-kind authorization at the external-handoff authority point after preparatory awaits, with an authoritative snapshot/version or conditional handoff that cannot admit a revocation already committed before handoff. Suppress without deleting inbox history or spending a provider attempt, and add delayed master/per-kind revocation controls. This extends the original send-time-consent finding; do not treat the earlier, narrower deferred-queue closure as blanket closure. ([Original B-648-9](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648#issuecomment-5965118899))

### C — follow-ups, not blockers for this piece

- **C-693-1:** `push-delivery.service.ts:234-254,487-496`: per-conversation collapse and per-user burst admission are check-then-write/read operations without shared per-user fencing; two replicas can both see no pending conversation, or both see seven prior sends, and independently create/send two rows. Code-derived counterexample, not an executed concurrent-DB proof. Follow-up rule: atomic conversation admission and shared burst reservations if the 8/10-minute limit is intended as a strict cross-replica invariant. ([Admission code](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fpush%2Fpush-delivery.service.ts))
- **C-693-2, outside this diff:** `notifications.service.ts:700-735,759-813` and legacy callers still bypass this outbox's quiet-copy/quiet-hours/receipt policy; drip and purchase continue calling that old path. Follow-up rule: a separately owned T4 unification preserving each caller's truthful delivered-versus-queued contract; do not claim all app notifications are protected by this PR. ([Legacy senders](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fnotifications%2Fnotifications.service.ts), [Legacy-call example](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20/src%2Fpackages%2Fdrip-dispatcher.cron.ts))

### Evidence and operator decisions

- Initial independent lane: **5 failed / 80 passed**; all four candidate delivery/emitter suites pass. Refined lane: **6 failed / 33 passed**, including 32 passing drip-dispatcher controls and the passing deletion-before-handoff control; six red assertions map to the four Bs above plus canonical **B-692-1** in P1. P1's privacy finding is recorded only on P1 and is not double-counted as a P2 B. ([Initial lane](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37343796456), [Refined lane](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37344206727))
- Candidate build/test, RLS floor/live, MWB/community live, audit and schema-parity checks pass at this head; **four main-only required gates have not run on the stacked P2** (CodeQL JS/TS, banned casts, SBOM, Danger), so this is not merge eligibility. ([Candidate CI](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37152425541), [P2 stack](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/693))
- Provider InvalidCredentials behavior, deadlines, durable receipts, current-zone deferral, and existing token-CAS controls pass in the candidate suites; no live Expo/device delivery is established. ([Replayed provider/policy tests](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37343796456))

No local heavy commands, PR-branch edits, merge, production access or deployment. Recommended default: fix the four Bs in P2 and B-692-1 in P1, restack, replay both lenses' probes, and require both exact-head verdicts plus all main-based gates before landing; retain FCM setup/real-device qualification before an Android delivery claim. Track Cs separately under the freeze. Nothing needed from the owner for these bounded fixes.

AUDIT Claude Opus 5.5 — growth-project-backend#693 @ 13417e7be58b96b6fccf203f71ec3b1f1ac8bb20 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

A/B/C = 0/1/9

Scope: P2 of the #648 split (outbox worker, send-time quiet hours and preferences, receipts, emitter wiring). Tree is identical to #648 @ 22de1182; #648 verdicts do not carry. Size 2,382 (grandfathered, 3,000 ceiling). CI at this head: green (non-main-base set). BEHIND main and conflicting (see C-693-2).

Checked and holding at this head:
- Preferences honoured at send time (master mute and per-kind toggle re-read before the handoff); quiet hours re-judged on a fresh clock after the reads and again after the handoff, in the recipient zone (resolveRecipientTimeZone, fallback to the row's zone).
- Outbox: (user_id, dedupe_key) unique for booking events; per-thread collapse for repeats; 429/5xx retried up to the cap; timeouts not resent (at most once); lease fencing via lease_token/handed_off_at.
- Receipts: DeviceNotRegistered clears only the exact token (ticket and receipt); receipts marked by compare-and-set; 30-day retention.
- No FCM key: InvalidCredentials keeps the token, records provider-not-configured, alerts at most hourly; no crash, no retry storm.
- Deletion: tombstone nulls the token; the manifest deletes the user's outbox rows.
- Live probes on Postgres 15 (all pass), run https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37345618739: L1 two workers on two pools drain 30 rows, each sent exactly once through the real `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claim; L2 five concurrent enqueues of one event leave one row; L3 a future row is not claimed, an unstarted lapsed lease is released and sent once, a handed-off lapsed lease is closed; L4 receipts read once across two replicas, DeviceNotRegistered clears only that token, old rows pruned. PR CI never ran this SQL on a database (only test/utils/push-outbox-fake.ts).

B-693-1 src/notifications/push/push-delivery.service.ts:540 — every outbox push is sent with `channelId: 'default'`. The mobile app creates only `coach-messages`, `client-bot`, `milestones`, `system` (growth-project-mobile src/notifications/push-channels.ts; mobile #341 adds none). Expo: "If an ID is specified but the corresponding channel does not exist on the device ... the notification will not be displayed to the user" (https://docs.expo.dev/push-notifications/sending-notifications/). Counterexample: once the FCM key is uploaded, every Android push from the outbox (messages, bookings, reminders, milestones, coach alerts) is accepted by Expo, recorded `sent` with a ticket, and never shown; coach alerts regress, since before this PR they went through pushToCoach with no channelId. Probe U1 fails at this head: channels sent = ["default","default","default"]. Fix rule: map kind to a channel the app creates (message -> coach-messages; booking and coach alert -> system; milestone -> milestones; reminders, nudges, build week -> client-bot) or omit channelId; pin the allowed set in a test.

C (follow-ups; FREEZE applies):
- C-693-2 Main refresh contract (conflict in src/notifications/notifications.service.ts CreateNotificationInput). Keep main's throttle_key, channelGate/gateFrom and describeFailure next to push_twin. Main's src/checkout/payout-notice.service.ts:445-455 (ee55f814) writes a push row beside its inapp row (:378-388) without push_twin, so each payout or refund notice stays twice in the coach inbox. Fix rule: set `push_twin: true` on that row in the refresh (operator decision).
- C-693-3 push-delivery.service.ts:324 and :446 — claim order is not_before only, and only reminders are re-checked at send. Probe U2 fails: "Session confirmed" deferred at 23:00 for a session cancelled overnight is still sent at 08:00. Fix rule: order by not_before, created_at, id; drop a deferred booking push when the session status no longer matches its kind.
- C-693-4 push-delivery.service.ts:610-617 — a connection refused before any request reached Expo is dropped as transport-error. Probe U3 fails (status dropped). Fix rule: treat connect-phase errors (ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT) as retryable.
- C-693-5 src/notifications/emitters/booking.emitter.ts:264-280 — rescheduled dedupe key is kind:session:newScheduledAt; A->B->A->B loses the last push. Fix rule: include oldScheduledAt in the key.
- C-693-6 src/scheduling/scheduling-session-lifecycle.service.ts:188, :281 — requested/declined pass created_at, not the session start, so they are never urgent (a 08:30 request made at 22:00 reaches the coach at 08:00). Fix rule: pass the session start in context.
- C-693-7 push-delivery.service.ts:245-249 — the collapse update ignores its count; a row claimed in between makes the new copy vanish. Fix rule: on count 0, insert a new row.
- C-693-8 outside this diff: src/users/users.service.ts:106-111 does not clear the same token from other users; with a best-effort sign-out, user A's pushes reach user B's device. Fix rule: clear expo_push_token = token on other users when registering.
- C-693-9 outside this diff: direct pushToUser/pushToCoach senders bypass the outbox, quiet hours and quiet copy (churn-intervention.service.ts:648 puts coach-written text on the lock screen; also dunning-v2.dispatcher.ts:169/282, coach-brief.scheduler.ts:402, coach-alerts.service.ts:244, workout-reminder.service.ts:302, nudge-engine.service.ts:417, drip-dispatcher.cron.ts:525, package-push.service.ts:734, purchase-fanout.service.ts:685, scout.service.ts:594). Fix rule: route through sendPush with quiet copy.
- C-693-10 Evidence: keep a live Postgres spec for the claim SQL in CI (pattern: probe L1-L4).

Release dependency: the client's zone comes from PUT /notifications/timezone (mobile #341, open); until it ships, clients fall back to their coach's zone.

FIX ROUND 5 (B-PUSH2-120, agent 120) — growth-project-backend#693 @ 53796f1e278c12ebb56d701724df032675dcedf1

MAIN REFRESH + FIX ROUND + RESTACK. First fix round on this PR (rounds 1-4 ran on #648 before the split). Answers Sol REQUEST CHANGES 0/4/2 (https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/693#issuecomment-5999124426) and Opus REQUEST CHANGES 0/1/9 (https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/693#issuecomment-5999369928). Normal pushes 13417e7b..c2cef1d1..53796f1e (no force, no rebase). Size 2,876 lines (+2,756/-120), 24 files against #692 @ 346cf4a8 (created 2026-10-03, grandfathered 3,000 ceiling).

## RESTACK (merge-only commits)
| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| 60fb8fe9 | merge #692 @ 32863d3c (main ee55f814 refresh). One conflict, `CreateNotificationInput` in `src/notifications/notifications.service.ts`: kept main's `throttle_key` and P2's `push_twin` side by side; main's channelGate/gateFrom/describeFailure kept as merged (Opus C-693-2 contract). |
| b2c167c6 | merge #692 @ 346cf4a8 (B-692-1 fix); no conflicts |

## Finding -> change -> commit
| Finding | Change | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| Opus B-693-1 Android channelId `default` | new `src/notifications/push/push-channels.ts`: the app's four channels (coach-messages, client-bot, milestones, system, as mobile `src/notifications/push-channels.ts` creates them); `androidChannelFor(kind)`: messages -> coach-messages, booking and coach-side kinds -> system, milestones and weight trend -> milestones, reminders, nudges, check-in, Build Week, assignments and drip -> client-bot, unknown -> system. The worker sends that channel. | c2cef1d1 |
| Sol B-693-1 reschedule dedupe | `BookingRescheduledPayload.rescheduleEventId` (optional); push dedupe `booking_rescheduled:<session>:<event id>`; the lifecycle service passes the session row's `updated_at` after the move, so the same move has one identity and a later move back to an earlier time has a new one; without an id the identity is `<old>><new>`. | c2cef1d1 |
| Sol B-648-7 hidden sole rows | `push_twin` hides a push row only when its inapp counterpart is found (same user, kind, deep link and text, stored in the last hour; a read error proves nothing, so the row stays visible). The drip and purchase writers pass `push_twin` only when their inapp write returned a row. | c2cef1d1 |
| Sol B-693-2 failed token clear settled | `clearToken` returns whether the exact-token clear ran. A failed clear is kept as `token-cleanup-pending` (ticket stage: dropped row with the token; receipt stage: receipt read, not counted). Each receipt sweep first retries those clears (oldest 100, the clear only, never the push) and settles them to `device-not-registered` with a CAS on the code. A token re-registered meanwhile is kept. | c2cef1d1 |
| Sol B-648-9 consent during preparation | after the handoff write, preferences and the device token are read again; a master mute or kind switch committed during preparation drops the row as `preference-off`, a sign-out as `no-token`, before anything reaches Expo; the inbox row is untouched. | c2cef1d1 |
| Sol B-692-1 (defense in depth) | the worker always renders the kind's template at send, with or without stored context; booking push context no longer stores display names. | c2cef1d1 |
| Opus C-693-2 (operator-approved, main refresh) | main's payout notice push row (`src/checkout/payout-notice.service.ts`) passes `push_twin: true`, so each notice is one inbox item (hidden only behind its inapp row). | c2cef1d1 |
| CI guard from the refresh | main's `test/privacy/no-pii-in-logs.spec.ts` flagged P2's `onModuleInit` log of a variable named `message`; renamed to `notWired` (same text). | 53796f1e |

## Tests at this head
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| test/push-delivery-round5.spec.ts (new, 15 cases: reschedule A>B>C>B and A>B>A>B with ids, same move twice; twin proof incl. switched-off inapp, different link, throttle_key + push_twin per payout notice, drip and purchase writers on inapp failure; token cleanup at receipt [0, 1] and at ticket with a re-registered token; mute, kind switch and sign-out during a 70 s preparation read plus controls; channel set and per-kind map; worker sends channel and template only) | 15/15 pass; with the src fix removed 12 of the first 14 cases fail (local) |
| Updated specs: push-delivery.service, push-delivery-send-time, booking-emitter, scheduling.service, s-fee-r5-or-111-1 (template copy, channel, no display name in context, event id, payout push_twin) | pass |
| `tsc --noEmit` (whole repo) and eslint on changed src | clean (local) |
| PR CI at 53796f1e | build-and-test (full suite) success: https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37352037508; every check that runs on this stacked PR is green (schema parity, rls, live suites, npm audit, size). Main-only gates (migrations forward/reversible, banned casts, CodeQL, danger) run when the base becomes main after #692 merges. |
| PR CI at c2cef1d1 | build-and-test failed only test/privacy/no-pii-in-logs.spec.ts (fixed in 53796f1e): https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37350492403 |

## Probe replay (both lenses)
Postgres CI lane at 53796f1e + both lenses' probe files: https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37352088482 (15 suites; 203/205; the two failures are Opus U2/U3, ruled follow-up Cs). Same result at c2cef1d1: https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37350591060.
| Lens | Probe | At 13417e7b | At 53796f1e |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sol P2 | distinct reschedules A -> B -> C -> B each reach the recipient once | fail | pass |
| Sol P2 | a suppressed inapp write is not proof that the sole push row is a twin | fail | pass |
| Sol P2 | the real drip writer preserves its sole push row when the inapp DB write fails | fail | pass |
| Sol P2 | a transient token-clear failure does not permanently settle a dead-device receipt | fail | pass |
| Sol P2 | mute committed during slow send preparation suppresses the external call | fail | pass |
| Sol P2 | the real message emitter does not expose private profile display-name text | fail | pass |
| Sol P2 | control: deleting outbox rows before the handoff prevents a stale send | pass | pass |
| Sol P1 | all 6 (message text, booking display name, health/unknown kinds, mute and switches, zoned quiet hours, receipt signal) | 4/6 (at #692 27156167) | 6/6 |
| Opus | U1 [B-693-1] every Android channelId is one the app creates | fail | pass |
| Opus | U2 [C-693-3] deferred "Session confirmed" for a session cancelled overnight | fail | fail (C, follow-up) |
| Opus | U3 [C-693-4] connection refused before Expo is retried | fail | fail (C, follow-up) |
| Opus | U4 [control] lock-screen copy has no health value or message text | pass | pass |
| Opus live | L1 two workers on two pools send each of 30 rows once (real claim SQL) | pass | pass |
| Opus live | L2 five concurrent enqueues of one event leave one row | pass | pass |
| Opus live | L3 not-yet-due row unclaimed; unstarted lapsed lease released and sent once | pass | pass |
| Opus live | L4 receipts read once across two replicas; DeviceNotRegistered clears only that token | pass | pass |
| Opus live | L5 erasure manifest entry | pass | pass |
| Opus live | L6 migration backfill hides only a proven twin | pass | pass |
| #648 rounds | B-648-8 stall before handoff, B-648-10 round-4 70 s read/handoff crossing, urgency and daytime controls (in push-delivery-send-time.spec.ts) | pass | pass |

## Money-list self-check
- Webhook order/redelivery: no webhook handler changed; the payout notice keeps its per-notice `throttle_key` and only gains `push_twin`.
- Concurrency and lock order: claim/lease SQL unchanged; new reads after the handoff are reads; token clear is a CAS on the exact token; cleanup settles by CAS on `result_code`; reschedule identity comes from the committed row.
- Terminal states: `token-cleanup-pending` never re-sends; it ends as `device-not-registered`; rows keep `sent`/`dropped` status.
- Pagination and fail-closed completeness: cleanup is bounded (100, oldest first) and repeats every sweep; a failed twin-proof read keeps the row visible; a failed consent read goes to the worker retry path without sending.
- Currency and minor units: no amount logic changed; no amounts on the lock screen.
- Copy truth: templates only on the lock screen (no names, notes, health values, first person, exclamation marks or emojis); Android channels match the app; Android delivery is unverified on device.

Follow-up Cs (not fixed, by ruling): Sol C-693-1 cross-replica collapse/burst admission; Sol C-693-2 legacy senders bypass the outbox; Opus C-692-2, C-693-3..C-693-10 (C-693-5 is closed by the reschedule fix). Merge order: #692 then #693 back to back; deploy after #693 with migrations.

READY FOR AUDIT
